topics.label: Lecture introduction and framing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture as an integration of previously learned immune cells and molecules.

topics.label: Principles of innate immune recognition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how innate immunity detects infection and damage through molecular patterns and appropriately positioned, germline-encoded receptors.

topics.label: Toll-like receptor recognition and signalling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how toll-like receptors translate microbial recognition into immune responses tailored to the location of the signal.

topics.label: Inflammatory activation through non-TLR sensing pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how innate sensing pathways beyond toll-like receptors activate inflammation and can contribute to inflammatory disease.

topics.label: Sentinel cells initiate inflammatory responses
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how activated sentinel cells produce signals whose reach determines whether inflammation remains local or becomes systemic.

topics.label: Recruiting leukocytes to infected tissue
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic follows the mechanism by which circulating leukocytes slow down, leave blood vessels, and reach the site of infection.

topics.label: Lymphatic transport and adaptive immune priming
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how the lymphatic drainage system enables activated dendritic cells to carry evidence of infection to lymph nodes for adaptive immune activation.

topics.label: Excessive inflammation and septic shock
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how excessive inflammatory activation produces dangerous systemic effects and septic shock.

topics.label: Mechanisms that resolve inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how inflammation is shut down through the changing balance between inflammatory stimulation and passive or active inhibition.

topics.label: Tissue repair and persistent inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine recovery of damaged tissue and explain why persistent inflammation can represent either failed restoration or protective containment of an unresolved infection.

topics.label: Lecture closing and next lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic ends the lecture and announces complement as the subject of the next lecture.
